props.title: True Lies
props.initialSlug: Secret agent juggles spy life and marriage chaos

sections.content: True Lies (1994) perfectly embodies James Cameron's knack for blending explosive action with character-driven storytelling. The film reinvented the spy thriller by injecting domestic comedy into its DNA, creating a unique hybrid that influenced films like Mr. & Mrs. Smith (2005) and Central Intelligence (2016). Arnold Schwarzenegger delivers one of his most nuanced performances, balancing the suave spy Harry Tasker with a bumbling family man persona, while Jamie Lee Curtis transforms from a bored housewife into an unlikely action hero, subverting typical 90s action movie gender roles.

sections.content: Cameron's direction elevates True Lies beyond typical 90s action fare through groundbreaking practical effects and stunt work. The Harrier jet sequence remains a masterclass in pre-CGI action filmmaking, while the horse-and-motorcycle chase through the Marriott Hotel showcases the director's commitment to practical stunts. This approach influenced later spy-action films like Casino Royale (2006) and Mission: Impossible - Fallout (2018), which similarly emphasized practical effects over CGI.

The film's humor sets it apart from contemporaries like Point Break (1991) and Speed (1994). Bill Paxton's car salesman character and Tom Arnold's sidekick provide genuine laughs without undermining the tension. This balance of comedy and action created a template followed by films like Kingsman: The Secret Service (2014) and Knight and Day (2010). SUBHEAD: The Evolution of the Action-Comedy Spy Film

sections.content: True Lies marked a significant shift in how Hollywood approached spy thrillers. Before this, films like The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) played it straight, while comedic spy films like Spies Like Us (1985) went full parody. Cameron found the sweet spot between these extremes, proving that action-comedy could work without sacrificing either element. This influenced modern hybrid successes like The Other Guys (2010) and 21 Jump Street (2012).
